title: Two Points of View · Teams
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Two Points of View · Teams with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Choose a simple fictional event involving two characters. The lead describes the event once from each character's viewpoint. Both descriptions refer to the same event and identify different viewpoints. Form two teams. Each team has four turns; only the lead’s teammates respond or assist. Each success earns the team one point. The higher team score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4–8 players; materials: None.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Two Points of View, what counts as a successful turn?
options: Both descriptions refer to the same event and identify different viewpoints.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
recall.why: Both descriptions refer to the same event and identify different viewpoints.
